page: Amazon Web Services m6a.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor clocked at 3.6 GHz, providing 4 vCPUs derived from 2 dedicated physical cores via simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is 16.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per vCPU). The instance architecture is x86_64, featuring 8 MB of L3 cache, hardware cryptographic extensions including AES and SHA-NI, but lacking AVX-512 and AMX instructions. It includes no local storage or GPUs, relying on remote block storage, and features a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread performance alongside constrained multi-core throughput due to the low physical core count. The instance achieves a top-25% result in stress-ng single-core tests (2991.79) and an average Geekbench single-core score of 1633.0. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics such as the stress-ng multi-core benchmark (5981.17) and Geekbench multi-core score (3703.0) fall into the bottom 25%. Similarly, large block memory bandwidth (37.49 GB/sec read, 22.1 GB/sec write) and passmark database operations (1920.42) are in the lower quartile, reflecting the limits of a 4-vCPU DDR4 memory subsystem.

From an architectural standpoint, the m6a.xlarge delivers cost-efficient general-purpose compute for medium-scale enterprise duties where high core counts and extreme I/O are unnecessary. Tradeoffs include the lack of bundled local NVMe storage and subdued throughput in heavy parallel operations such as Clang compilation, ray tracing, and 7B-parameter LLM inference. It is primarily fit for mid-tier web serving, small background workers, microservices, light data preprocessing, and general-purpose development or staging environments.
description: Amazon Web Services m6a.xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.6 GHz. It offers 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory, providing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the server excludes integrated local storage and GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage and offering a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU execution, achieving a top-quartile stress-ng score, but multi-threaded processing, memory bandwidth, and multi-core Geekbench metrics reflect lower-tier performance dictated by the 4-thread envelope. Lacking AVX-512 capabilities and bundled disks, the m6a.xlarge trades high-intensity parallel processing for reliable baseline CPU capability, making it well matched for standard web applications, small microservices, CI/CD execution nodes, and low-scale application backends.
